articles.title: 5 reasons Deion Sanders and Colorado might actually be good in 2026
articles.summary: Colorado coach Deion Sanders has said he has a 'pretty good football team' this year and his best coaching staff ever. He might actually be right.
articles.body:
Before he started his third season at Colorado in 2025, coach Deion Sanders proclaimed he had assembled his best team ever .

Then the Buffaloes finished with a 3-9 record .

This year, he says he has a " pretty good football team " along with his " best coaching staff " ever.

College football season predictions: Picks for CFP, Heisman, biggest surprises

The experts and oddsmakers don't and are picking his team to finish near the bottom of the Big 12 .

But I do believe him and am picking Colorado to finish among the top 3 in the league, along with Texas Tech and BYU. Here are five reasons as the Buffs prepare to open the season Thursday, Sept. 3 at Georgia Tech (8 p.m. ET; ESPN).

Sanders deserves credit for innovating and adjusting in the age of unlimited annual player transfers. He was the first transfer portal king in 2023 before it was considered cool in college football. This year, he entered the summer with 41 new scholarship transfers from other four-year colleges, including 23 from outside the Power Four conferences, according to CU records.

In a change from before, Sanders favored production over potential with this group, much like Indiana did last year on its run to the national championship. Of those 23 transfers from the lower rungs of Division I, 16 are former starters.

That list doesn't even count wide receiver transfer Kam Perry, a walk-on who started 12 games last year at Miami (Ohio) and made 43 catches for 976 yards.

2. Offensive coordinator Brennan Marion has the edge

Marion is Sanders' third offensive coordinator in four seasons but also the edgiest since the Buffs shocked the nation with a 3-0 start under then-offensive coordinator Sean Lewis in 2023.

Marion's Go-Go offense is eclectic enough to spin the heads of opposing defenses and has averaged at least 33 points per game since 2023, when he was offensive coordinator at UNLV.

His background and leadership pedigree also make him a potential successor to Sanders someday, continuing the upward climb he's been making ever since he was homeless in junior college and slept under the bleachers of the stadium .

Colorado started three quarterbacks last year, which is another way of saying they didn't have any good enough for Sanders. Lewis was one of those starters for two of those games but was only 18 years old as a touted freshman out of Georgia. This is his moment. He compiled a 39-4 record as a three-year starter in high school and has the potential to lead Colorado to a special season if he adjusts well to Marion's offense early on.

Marion has said Lewis has a " million-dollar arm " and especially wants to win the season opener in his home state.

"He understands how to win a football game," Marion said Aug. 27.

This time, he'll benefit from a big, beefy offensive line averaging well over 300 pounds apiece, plus a crew of talented receivers, including Texas transfer DeAndre Moore.

The Buffs made a clean break from last year, when they ranked 135 th out of 136 major college teams in rushing yards allowed per game with 222.5. They have a new defensive coordinator (Chris Marve), new cornerbacks coach ( Aaron Fletcher ), new defensive line coach (Dante Carter) and new safeties coach ( Vonn Bell ) to go with an all-new starting lineup. It features playmakers who have drawn raves, including Tennessee transfer defensive back Boo Carter and Notre Dame transfer cornerback Cree Thomas.

Sanders especially praised his linebackers, which include Texas transfer Liona Lefau.

"I can't say enough about them," Sanders said Aug. 14. "They're extraordinary. They're probably the best position group on this team."

Texas Tech once again has the best roster that money can buy in the Big 12. BYU also has the stars to compete for the Big 12 title, just like the Cougars did in 2024 and 2025. But after that, who really knows with so many players changing teams every year? Why not Colorado?

Sanders has been up and down in Boulder to the extreme — a 3-0 start in 2023, followed by a 1-8 finish, then a 9-4 season in 2024 and a 3-9 season in 2025. The prediction here is the pendulum is swinging back, especially with expectations so low now outside of Colorado.

On the other hand, what happens if the Buffs get crushed in their opener in Atlanta? Their season could plunge downhill from there with two of their next three games on the road. But a win there could have the opposite effect, and this team is too improved to let that happen anyway.

Follow reporter Brent Schrotenboer @Schrotenboer . Email: bschrotenb@usatoday.com

articles.title: Cowboys' Von Miller lands No. 40 by making Luepke a business partner
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboy recent acquisition Von Miller has No. 40, but he had to give Hunter Luepke more than a lifetime supply of chicken to get it.
articles.body:
The funniest subplot of the Dallas Cowboys' preseason has been resolved. Von Miller now owns No. 40 and Hunter Luepke owns part of a chicken farm.

Shortly after Dallas signed the free agent and future Hall of Famer Miller, he revealed he wanted to wear the No. 40 that he wore at DeSoto High School (Dallas area) and at Texas A&M, with the snag that it was already held by the fullback Luepke.

To that end Miller, the co-founder and co-owner of the organic poultry farm Greener Pastures Chicken, offered Luepke a lifetime supply of chicken . He may have underestimated Luepke's bargaining skills and now Luepke is evidently a business partner.

"Being the great negotiator he is, he was like, 'How about equity in Greener Pastures Chicken?'" Miller said on his Free Range podcast. "I was like, 'It's something that we could probably work out.' … 'We kind of had to do some negotiating at first. He's been 40 for a long time. It ain't something that I can just come in and Boss Hogg."

Miller said he was 90% certain he had a deal, and now it's 100%, official. Miller is in No. 40 and Luepke is moving to No. 30. This may come as a relief to anyone who bought a $150 Von Miller jersey . The amount of equity he received is undisclosed, but there is likely plenty of chicken in the future for both of them.

In other news, Caleb Downs is now officially in the No. 13 he has worn for most of the preseason.

Bret Bloomquist can be reached, bbloomquist@elpasotimes.com; @Bretbloomquist on X.

articles.title: Yankees expected to make Brian Cashman job decision that should not be a surprise
articles.summary: The Yankees' front office exec seems like he's got a safe seat in New York.
articles.body:
As the 2026 season winds down, plenty of manager and front office positions are going to open around the league. Some are already open, and teams are looking to make some new hires.

But what about the New York Yankees ? They would obviously keep their power structure intact if they win the World Series, but in general, regardless of the season outcome, what are the Yankees most likely to do?

According to MLB insider Robert Murray of Fansided.com , the Yankees are expected to keep Brian Cashman, along with Aaron Boone, as both of their jobs are seemingly very safe regardless of the outcome of the 2026 Yankees season.

Yankees expected to keep Brian Cashman regardless of 2026 season outcome

"But both Cashman and Boone have done a very good job in New York. Cashman is a surefire Hall of Fame executive," Murray writes. "... I firmly expect both to remain with the Yankees beyond the 2026 season. They do not feel like they are in any danger of being let go."

The Yankees are currently contending for the AL East title, though the Tampa Bay Rays have a solid lead that, unless Aaron Judge returns from injury, might be too difficult to catch up to.

Cashman received some flak for bringing back a lot of their players this offseason, with the Trent Grisham qualifying offer decision also not being well received.

The same went for the trade deadline, as Cashman didn't exactly receive resounding praise for his addition of Heliot Ramos, and the lack of some extra bullpen help or a new catcher.

But the re-signing of Cody Bellinger, the trade for Ryan Weathers, and the trade for Luis Garcia Jr. at the MLB trade deadline were all great moves that have helped and will help the Yankees this season.

While there might be some Yankees fans frustrated with Cashman's roster construction, Murray wholeheartedly believes that Cashman isn't going to be leaving the Yankees now, or anytime soon.

Sure, he might've made some mistakes over the offseason, but every executive and general manager in every professional sports league does. Cashman has made mistakes, but he's more than made up for it with high-quality moves during his tenure.

Neither Cashman nor Boone is expected to be let go at the end of the season, according to Murray. This shouldn't surprise any Yankees fans, as Cashman is practically locked in as long as he wants the job.

articles.title: So, that J.J. McCarthy Trade Rumor Did Get an Answer (Sort Of)
articles.summary: Nolan Teasley was asked about possibly trading J.J. McCarthy. Given that it’s a pertinent topic, the question is a good […]
articles.body:
Nolan Teasley was asked about possibly trading J.J. McCarthy . Given that it's a pertinent topic, the question is a good one to ask (at least if you ask me).

Part of the problem is that Mr. Teasley didn't appear particularly keen about digging into the issue . His answer about whether teams had been calling: "That's something I'll probably keep internal. We get calls all the time but it's not something I would directly comment on [in] regards to any player." Teasley, in short, opts to keep his cards close to his chest. Maybe teams called; maybe teams didn't. All that he's saying is that front offices talk commonly about trades but he wouldn't go any further.

Does J.J. McCarthy Get Sent Packing Via Trade?

Of course, the possibility remains that Mr. McCarthy will get sent packing. Any trade needs a pair of partners to do business.

Presumably, there are teams out there willing to send out a draft pick(s) to snag the 23-year-old quarterback. The issue is simply that nobody in their right mind would hand over anything close to what the Vikings had to pay to get him in the first place: the No. 10 selection in the 2024 NFL Draft.

Minnesota can therefore hang onto the young fella or sell for pennies on the dollar.

In his column earlier today, Jeff Diamond wrote about the McCarthy trade issue .

"If another team offered a first round pick for McCarthy," Diamond writes, "it would be hard to pass up. That's certainly not going to happen after his injury-prone and inconsistent play last year (although he did end the season with better play and four straight wins) and in preseason this year with his accuracy still a major concern."

More from Diamond: "There's no way Teasley and O'Connell would trade McCarthy for the minimal return of probably a fourth round pick at this point (which is what the 49ers received from the Cowboys for Trey Lance in 2023 and Lance was the third overall pick in 2021 but was often hurt and inconsistent and he was beat out for the starting job by Brock Purdy)."

Similarly of note is the work of Tom Rudelius, a math nerd who ventured into the precedent of recent NFL history to gauge what J.J. McCarthy could demand on the trade market .

After spilling some digital ink, Rudelius writes that "it's hard to imagine that McCarthy could net more than a 5th Round pick at this point. Part of the reason why the price for former 1st Round QBs has dropped in recent years is probably because none of the QBs in the table above have brought any meaningful value to the team that traded for them."

Would Nolan Teasley move on from J.J. McCarthy if the offer involved recouping a 4th or 5th? That's a good question, but it's hard to know if there has even been some trade discussions happening at all.

In 2025, McCarthy went 6-4 as Minnesota's starting quarterback. Pushing his team to that winning record came despite completing a horrible 57.6% of his passes while only climbing up to 1,632 yards and 11 touchdowns. Keep in mind that he had 12 interceptions alongside 6 fumbles.

At 23, J.J. McCarthy still has a lot of football in front of him. Whether that football gets played in the North Star State is an open question.

articles.title: Cowboys strip their best player of Captain's C, announce 2026 crew
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys have voted for their new captains, but a top player isn't returning to the captain's chair.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys had a unique approach to their game-day captains under former head coach Mike McCarthy. Each week, the team would designate new captains, leading to many players holding the honor, but losing the weekly accountability from having season-long designations. Brian Schottenheimer changed that to a more traditional structure in his first season, naming two captains from each unit.

Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb were captains for the offense, Donovan Wilson and Osa Odighizuwa were captains for the defense, and Brandon Aubrey and CJ Goodwin wore the "C" for the special teams unit. Three of those players, Wilson, Odighizuwa and Goodwin, are no longer on the team, opening up the opportunity for new names to join the fold. But it's not the names which are added that are noteworthy; it's a name that's been removed.

Prescott is the sole designation for the offense, meaning that after sporting the C for all of 2025, Lamb is no longer one of the offense's captains. Whether or not this is a significant development is in the eyes of the beholder, but with the front office continuously chirping about their inability to pay top dollar for both Lamb and wideout George Pickens beyond this season, it's an interesting change.

To be clear, this isn't a coach's decision; the players vote on the captains each year.

Lamb, who was recently named the NFC East's best player by ESPN , has two years remaining on his contract beyond this one, while Pickens is playing on the franchise tag for 2026.

Meanwhile, the team has kept Aubrey as the special teams captain, and named the starting defensive interior as co-captains for the defense. Quinnen Williams, acquired in a deadline trade last year, received a hefty extension this year, cementing his role as the centerpiece of the defense moving forward. He's joined in the captain's room by Kenny Clark, the defense's elder statesman prior to the late-camp signing of Von Miller.

In a nutshell, the team voted for the players with the biggest paychecks and most responsibility from each unit, along with the returning player with the most skins on the wall.

articles.title: Ohio State hosting Jaxson Davis, Deng Ngor on official visits
articles.summary: As the first home football game of 2026 approaches, here's which 2027 prospects the Ohio State men's basketball team will host during the weekend.
articles.body:
During the first home football game at Ohio State this season, the Buckeyes men's basketball team will host two prospects on official visits.

When OSU hosts Ball State on Sept. 5 at Ohio Stadium, coach Jake Diebler will bring two players from the class of 2027 along for the experience.

It's still unclear how many players Ohio State might sign for its 2027 class. The Buckeyes had a commitment from five-star guard LJ Smith , but he graduated early and is getting his freshman season started with the Buckeyes. Of the 15 players currently on Ohio State's roster, the only one known to be out of eligibility after this season is fifth-year guard Jimmie Williams .

Otherwise, all 14 other players would have the ability to still be on the roster for 2027-28. Granted, that scenario is highly unlikely in the era of name, image and likeness rights, but it does decrease the likelihood of Ohio State signing a big 2027 class.

Here are the two prospects Ohio State will be hosting on official visits during the weekend of Aug. 4-6.

Listed at 6-foot, 165 pounds, Davis is a four-star point guard originally from Chicago who will play his senior season at Kansas City (Kansas) Monarch Academy. He is the No. 41 national prospect in the 247Sports.com composite, the No. 9 point guard in the country and the No. 1 player in Kansas.

This is expected to be the first of four visits for Davis. He is scheduled to go to Minnesota on Sept. 11, Iowa on Sept. 19 and Michigan State on Oct. 1.

The 6-8, 200-pound power forward has made a significant rise in the 247Sports recruiting rankings this summer. Ngor was listed as the No. 150 national prospect until late August, and when the rankings refreshed, he was up to No. 55.

A senior at Fort Erie (Ontario) International Academy, Ngor also has planned visits to see Washington on Sept. 18, Florida on Sept. 22 and Duke on Oct. 15.

articles.title: Packers to wear 1923 throwback uniforms in Week 14 vs. Bills
articles.summary: The Packers will wear their 1923 Classic throwback uniform in Week 14 against the Bills.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers will wear their "1923 Classic" throwback uniforms in Week 14 against the Buffalo Bills.

The uniform, which debuted last season, features brown, hand-painted faux leather helmets, navy jerseys with gold numbers and stripes, and tan colored pants. The Packers lost to the Carolina Panthers at Lambeau Field while debuting the uniforms in November of last year.

According to the Packers, the throwback uniform is "inspired by what the team wore in 1923, its first season as a publicly owned corporation."

articles.title: Newcastle United vs Bournemouth: Match Preview, Latest Team News and Score Prediction
articles.summary: Newcastle vs Bournemouth Preview: Jaissle and Rose Face Early Premier League TestTwo games are a poor basis for grand conclusions, but they are enough to spo...
articles.body:
Newcastle vs Bournemouth Preview: Jaissle and Rose Face Early Premier League Test

Two games are a poor basis for grand conclusions, but they are enough to spot trends. Newcastle United look sharper, quicker and more coherent than plenty expected after a summer of change. Bournemouth have been competitive too, but they are still paying for late lapses. That is the backdrop to this Premier League meeting, a game that already feels useful in measuring where both clubs are heading.

There was understandable anxiety around Newcastle after major upheaval, particularly with Matthias Jaissle replacing Eddie Howe and several familiar names moving on. So far, the response has been strong. A 2-2 draw against Liverpool could easily have been more, then came a deserved 2-0 win away at Tottenham. That is not noise. That is evidence.

Bournemouth also changed direction in the dugout after Andoni Iraola left for Liverpool, with Marco Rose taking charge. The performances have had substance, the outcomes less so. A 2-1 defeat at Manchester City came after they led 1-0, and a 1-1 draw against Everton was spoiled by a late equaliser. It is the kind of start that leaves a manager encouraged by the process and irritated by the details.

Jaissle has injuries to deal with across the pitch. Dan Burn is out with an ankle and foot issue, Joelinton is sidelined by a thigh problem, and William Osula is also unavailable because of an ankle and foot injury. Tino Livramento has returned to training after calf surgery, but this match may come too soon.

That puts more focus on the midfield pairing. Nico Gonzalez started against Spurs and looks set to continue alongside Lewis Miley. It gives Newcastle control and legs in the middle, and right now that matters. Summer arrival Matias Fernandez-Pardo, signed from Lille, is expected to start on the bench, which is sensible rather than cautious.

Further forward, Newcastle have threat. Yoane Wissa has started the season well after an injury-hit first campaign at the club, and his goal at Spurs underlined why he can be central to this side. He is direct, he attacks space early, and he does not need much invitation.

Bournemouth's summer was defined more by retention than recruitment, and there is value in that. Keeping quality players matters. Alex Scott remains the reference point in midfield after scoring against Everton, and his job will be to feed Evanilson, with Marcus Tavernier, Justin Kluivert and Rayan operating behind him.

There are absentees here too. Junior Kroupi, Julian Araujo, Amine Adli and Veljko Milosavljevic remain unavailable. Even so, Rose has enough attacking quality to cause Newcastle problems, particularly if the game opens up in transition.

Tavernier is one to watch. He scored against Manchester City and may have penalty duties. In a match where both sides carry attacking intent, that matters.

This is a tough call because the margins have been thin for both clubs. Newcastle have looked the more convincing side through two matches, and they carry momentum after winning at Spurs. Bournemouth have enough craft and speed to score, but they keep leaving the door open.

So the blunt verdict is simple. Expect chances, expect spells of control from both teams, and expect this to be close.

articles.title: A closer look at newest Saints tight end Stone Smartt
articles.summary: New Saints practice squad tight end Stone Smartt has the versatility that could benefit the offense as a developmental project
articles.body:
One of the roster changes made by the New Orleans Saints since roster cutdowns on Sunday was adding another tight end. Fourth-year veteran Stone Smartt was a waiver claim by the Saints for their practice squad.

Awarded No. 84 upon his arrival, Smartt is joined on the practice squad by tight end Treyton Welch, re-signed by New Orleans on Wednesday. Here's a closer look at Smartt, the team's newest tight end.

New Orleans Saints at Dallas Cowboys: Best photos of preseason Week 3

A state championship quarterback at Del Oro High School in California, Smartt would be recruited to play quarterback at Northern Arizona. He'd transfer to River City Community College after one year with next to no action. After one year as a JUCO All-American, Smartt then transferred to Old Dominion. He was the quarterback for the Monarchs in 2019, completing 57.1% of his passes for 1,006 yards with 1 touchdown, 6 interceptions, and 181 rushing yards with another 5 scores. In 2021, Smartt moved to wide receiver. That year, he'd pull in 17 receptions for 167 yards.

Smartt was not selected in the 2022 NFL Draft, instead signing on with the Los Angeles Chargers. Head coach of the Chargers at that time was Brandon Staley, defensive coordinator for the Saints. Staley would coach Smartt into his second year with the Chargers. Offensive coordinator for the Chargers that second season in 2023 was Kellen Moore, now head coach of New Orleans.

As a rookie in 2022, Smartt appeared in seven games with one start, catching 4 passes for 17 yards. In 2023, he'd appear in 16 games with three starts, playing in what remains a career-best 309 offensive snaps. Smartt would have 11 receptions for 155 yards, catching his first career touchdown. He'd have 16 catches for 208 yards in 2024, his career-high in both categories to this point.

Smartt was signed by the New York Jets during 2025 free agency. He'd appear in 15 games and catch 7 balls for 52 yards. This offseason, Smartt was signed by the Philadelphia Eagles in free agency but released on Aug. 29. The Saints signed him three days later after roster cutdowns throughout the NFL.

Smartt is expected to start 2026 on the practice squad. New Orleans has three talented tight ends in Juwan Johnson, Noah Fant, and rookie Oscar Delp. However, Smartt may get a look on special teams at some because of his athleticism. He's played 445 snaps on the special teams units over the last three seasons. A former high school and college quarterback, Smartt also has some versatility to go along with his athletic skills that could be beneficial to the Saints offense as a developmental player.

articles.title: Blue Jays beat Guardians 6-3 to close within a half-game of the final AL wild-card spot
articles.summary: Brett Bateman had three hits, Nathan Lukes lined a two-run double with the bases loaded in the fifth inning and the Toronto Blue Jays moved within striking d...
articles.body:
CLEVELAND (AP) — Brett Bateman had three hits, Nathan Lukes lined a two-run double with the bases loaded in the fifth inning and the Toronto Blue Jays moved within striking distance of the third AL wild-card spot with a 6-3 victory over the Cleveland Guardians on Thursday.

Toronto (70-71) has won five of six and is a half-game behind Cleveland (70-70) after taking two of three in the series. The Blue Jays also won four of six in the season series.

Tanner Bibee took a major league-leading 15th loss for the Guardians. Austin Hedges had a two-run, bases-loaded single in the fifth inning to get Cleveland within 5-3.

Angel Genao came up as the potential tying run with runners on first and second and two outs in the ninth, but Louis Varland struck him out to pick up his 32nd save in 33 opportunities. Spencer Miles (6-2) got the win.

The game was tied at 1 before Toronto sent 10 to the plate in its four-run fifth.

Ernie Clement and Brandon Valenzuela drew walks before Bateman got aboard with a bunt single down the third-base line to load the bases. Bibee (5-15) decided to make a play on the bunt, even though it appeared as if it was going to roll foul. Lukes then followed with the go-ahead hit.

Bibee, who gave up five runs on four hits, tied a career high with five walks in four-plus innings.

Toronto starter José Soriano allowed three runs on six hits in 4 2/3 innings.

Blue Jays: Head to Kansas City for a weekend series. RHP Jameson Taillon (2-6, 5.68 ERA) will start on Friday.

Guardians: Have a split doubleheader against Detroit on Friday to start a four-game set. Game 1's starter has not been determined. LHP Foster Griffin (15-4, 3.21 ERA) is expected to go in the nightcap.

articles.title: We want Fury v Joshua at Wembley - London mayor
articles.summary: London Mayor Sadiq Khan says he is "really keen" to host the proposed Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua fight at Wembley Stadium and has urged promoters to get in to...
articles.body:
London Mayor Sadiq Khan says he is "really keen" to host the proposed Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua fight at Wembley Stadium and has urged promoters to get in touch.

BBC Sport understands Saudi organisers Sela have contacted the mayor's office in recent weeks about bringing the long-awaited contest to the national stadium.

However, with organisers and broadcaster Netflix understood to favour New York's Madison Square Garden for a November bout, sources close to the discussions say talks over a London venue have not progressed, with no detailed talks over dates or timings.

"A message to the promoters - we want to host it in London. Talk to us, we're really keen to have it," Khan told BBC Sport on Thursday.

Wembley Stadium's usual curfew is 23:00, although Khan has previously indicated he would support efforts to bring the fight to London.

A late-night fight in London - potentially in the early hours - could mean it draws a larger television audience in the US.

Brent Council, the local authority involved in any approval, has said a potential extension of the curfew would need to be assessed by Wembley's safety advisory group.

It remains unclear how late that curfew could be pushed back.

"Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury are two great British boxers. Both have been world champions," Khan said.

"They both recognise and love the fans in this country who have supported them throughout their careers, amateur and professional.

"Wembley has hosted many fantastic events, including bouts involving Tyson and Anthony. We, the fans, want to see them box live in London."

There is hope that the venue will be finalised in the coming days. Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn has said he wants an announcement this week, with a news conference to follow next week.

BBC Sport has contacted Sela for comment.

Hearn says his side signed a contract for the bout to take place in the United Kingdom, while Sela and Netflix's preference would be the United States, to cater for American audiences.

Matchroom Boxing's Hearn has previously said Joshua's contract specifically stipulated a UK venue and would need to be renegotiated for the fight to take place Stateside.

Hearn says he has since set out terms under which Matchroom would agree to the change, with negotiations continuing over a possible move to New York.

The contact from Sela represents a significant development from the end of July, when sources close to the mayor told BBC Sport there had been no approach from the fight's organisers.

But the lack of progress since that initial contact underlines the uncertainty still surrounding Wembley's chances of hosting the contest.

"I'm hoping the promoters understand that not only will you get 100,000 people watching this bout live, you'll get millions watching it across the globe, where both boxers are cheered on by their loyal fans," Khan said.
authors: Kal Sajad - BBC Sport boxing journalist

articles.title: Cubs Lose 1.85 Pitcher For Rest Of Season
articles.summary: The Chicago Cubs have been waiting for Ben Brown to return, but his season is over
articles.body:
The Chicago Cubs have been waiting for Ben Brown to return from his neck injury, but his season is over, according to Cubs insider Taylor McGregor .

Brown was trying to come back and provide some much-needed help for the Cubs pitching staff. He originally went on the injured list in June. However, after a bridge camp game in late August, he once again started experiencing symptoms of his neck injury.

That setback ultimately sealed his fate. Without Brown coming back, the Cubs will have to rely on the arms they have and potentially some other returning arms. Shelby Miller, Edward Cabrera, Javier Assad and Justin Steele could still come and save the Cubs' pitching staff.

The biggest issue for the Cubs has been the bullpen. The Cubs bullpen has a 4.02 ERA on the season, and in the second half, the bullpen has allowed 1.22 home runs per nine innings, ranked eighth-worst in baseball.

Brown was a swingman who could have started games if the Cubs needed him as well. He had a 1.85 ERA in 20 games this season. He had made eight starts and covered a total of 68 innings. He was having a great season, bouncing back from his 5.92 ERA last year.

The Cubs are suddenly in danger of falling out of the postseason entirely. They have lost 12 of their last 19 games and hold a 4 1/2 game lead in the wild card race. Winning the division seems extremely unlikely right now, as they sit nine games back of the Milwaukee Brewers. If they do not start playing better baseball soon, their lead in the wild card race will evaporate as the Arizona Diamondbacks and San Diego Padres close in.

articles.title: GB's Dart struggles with illness in second-round exit
articles.summary: Britain's Harriet Dart says she felt "under the weather" as she struggles in the heat during her second-round loss to Marie Bouzkova at the US Open.
articles.body:
Britain's Harriet Dart said she felt "under the weather" as she struggled in the heat during her second-round loss to Marie Bouzkova at the US Open.

Dart struggled for rhythm in a 6-2 6-2 defeat by Czech 25th seed Bouzkova as temperatures reached around 30C in New York.

Dart's defeat means Fran Jones is the last remaining Briton in either singles draw at Flushing Meadows.

Jones faces American 14th seed Iva Jovic later on Thursday.

Dart draped ice towels around her neck and used cold-air hoses at the changeovers against Bouzkova as she attempted to cool down.

"I have been a bit under the weather. It is what it is, sadly," Dart, 30, said.

"It was quite warm. I had a temperature, I was trying to cool down. I've played many weeks in a row.

"I am not used to air conditioning being pumped everywhere. We go from really hot outside to freezing inside.

"All credit to my opponent, she is an incredibly tough player, so even if I had been at full capacity, I don't know."

Dart, who is ranked 131st in the world, struggled on serve against Bouzkova, committing eight double faults and landing only 45% of her first serves.

Bouzkova took command almost straight away, winning seven games in a row to clinch the first set and go a double break up in the second.

From there Dart was unable to recover as Bouzkova safely saw out the rest of the match to reach the third round, where she will face Polish eighth seed Iga Swiatek.

Dart's exit follows compatriot Katie Boulter's second-round defeat by Karolina Muchova in only 58 minutes on Wednesday.

In the men's draw, Jacob Fearnley and Toby Samuel lost in the second round, while Cameron Norrie, Arthur Fery, Harry Wendelken and Jan Choinski exited in the first round.

articles.title: Aryna Sabalenka Snaps at Reporter During US Open Press Conference: ‘Think Before You Say Stuff’
articles.summary: Aryna Sabalenka takes her sport very seriously. After defeating Polina Iatcenko in the second round of the US Open in New York City on Wednesday, September 2...
articles.body:
Aryna Sabalenka takes her sport very seriously.

After defeating Polina Iatcenko in the second round of the US Open in New York City on Wednesday, September 2, the Belarusian tennis star, 28, was asked by a reporter about her "mood now that the tournament has started," in a press conference posted on YouTube .

"Obviously, last week it's lots of parties and fun and stuff like that," the reporter noted.

Sabalenka shook her head and interrupted, "You guys are, like, a joke. Parties, fun… like, why would ⁠you even say that? Why would ​you ⁠even think about that? Like, what kind of question is that?"

"Just because I posted, like, some activities with brands , and you think that I've been partying, not training?" the two-time US Open champ continued.

"I'm not saying you go to the parties and that you're…." the reporter tried to clarify.

"You literally said that," the No. 1 seed snapped, before adding, "Next question."

"For everyone who is unclear, I'm not suggesting that Aryna is having fun at these parties," the reporter continued.

"Thanks yeah," Sabalenka responded. "OK. Move on."

The reporter then tried to rephrase his question. "So now that the tournament has started, do you find you're getting quite serious and combative?"

"Oh, yeah, I wasn't serious before that. Next question," the clearly irritated athlete replied quickly.

As the next reporter began to speak, she blurted, "Think before you say stuff."

Sabalenka will face Kamilla Rakhimova in the third round on Friday, September 4.

articles.title: Michigan football schedule for 2027 gets update, including Texas game
articles.summary: College Football Week 0 will be eliminated and the entire FBS will open prior to Labor Day weekend. Here's the Michigan football 2027 schedule update.
articles.body:
Michigan football has tweaked its schedule for the 2027 season.

What has recently been known as "Week 0" has been eliminated and now the entire Football Bowl Subdivision will open its season prior to Labor Day weekend 2027.

As a result, Michigan's season opener against Buffalo has been moved to Aug. 28, its Week 2 matchup at Texas has been moved to Sept. 4 (previously Sept. 11) and the Wolverines will wrap up their nonconference season Sept. 11 against Eastern Michigan in Ann Arbor.

There was concern earlier this week after a report that U-M's game vs. EMU had been moved to the previously scheduled date with Texas, but a team spokesman told the Free Press it was simply the required schedule shuffling with the season being moved up and the big time matchup in Austin would be on as scheduled.

This also means Michigan will have two bye weeks in the 2027 season, though those dates (like the rest of the schedule) are still to be determined.

Michigan's return trip to Texas represents the back half of a home-and-home with the Longhorns . The first matchup came in 2024, when UT came to Ann Arbor and beat U-M 31-12 in Week 2.

This will mark the third time the two sides meet in the span of four seasons − the Longhorns beat the Wolverines 41-27 in the Cheez-It Citrus Bowl in Orlando, Fla. on Dec. 31, 2025, in a game coached by interim coach Biff Poggi, less than one week after Kyle Whittingham was named Michigan's new head man.

Tony Garcia is the Michigan beat writer for the Detroit Free Press. Email him at apgarcia@freepress.com and follow him on X at @RealTonyGarcia .
